content:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a sensitivity sweep for Dedicated pool sizing for the ACME Retail pilot (us-west2). results look non-linear when we reduce committed throughput by ~15-25% during their evening spike.

sam: spreadsheet: https://tinyurl.com/rdw-ded-sens (summary tab + raw sim). I pushed the sim job to the canary cluster this morning.

kai: TL;DR — if we size for 80% of observed peak (instead of 100%), prefix cache hit rate drops ~8% and tail latency (p95) jumps from 280ms -> ~520ms for the 30% of requests that miss cache. overall token cost drops ~9% but SLA risk goes up.

anita: what cost assumptions did you use? committed discount tiers, preemptible fallbacks, and burst pricing?

sam: assumptions in the sheet: committed tier = 1.0x baseline (no additional discount), burst backing is on-demand (1.6x unit cost), preemptible only for non-SLA traffic. also modeled 2 minute cold-start penalty for new VMs.

maya: pasted minimal sim config for reference:

```
pool_size: 18 gpus
committed_tp: 80k req/min
burst_pool: 6 gpus
cache_policy: prefix_kv (24h TTL)
workload_shape: weekday-evening spike (x1.9 peak)
cost_model: committed=1.0, on_demand=1.6, preemptible=0.35
```

kai: important note — the evening spike has a heavy long-context tail which amplifies KV cache miss cost. our sim used a mixed sequence length distribution; if ACME shifts more long-context calls, impact worsens.

anita: can we add a conservative knob: commit 90% of expected peak + 10% burst buffer reserved for SLA traffic, and charge a slightly higher unit for bursts? customers expect predictability.

billing-bot: invoice-alert: acct-ACME projected monthly overage if committed=80k -> +$12,400 estimated (30-day projection based on sim).

sam: proposal: run a 48h replay using actual ACME request traces (sanitized) across us-west2 and eu-west1, test three commit points: 70%, 85%, 100% of recorded peak. include cold-start noise, and log per-route p95/p99.

maya: agree. next steps: @sam to kick off replay + add per-route SLIs to the output; @kai to add sequence-length sensitivity to the sim; @anita to draft pricing note with burst unit and overage terms. we should reconvene after the 48h run. :thumbsup:

sam: started the replay job, job id rdw-sim-2024-11-06-17. will post logs and a link to the results channel when done.

maya: thanks — if the 85% run meets SLAs we can prepare a recommended commit tier for ACME and a conservative billing guardrail.

kai: noted. will also add a quick script to compute break-even cost point for preemptible vs on-demand for burst usage.

anita: rough ETA 72h for pricing note after we have replay outputs.

maya: closing loop here — marking action items in the sheet. ping if you need quota or test cluster increases.
